embeddedReportPolicy: Original reports embedded in full, without rewriting findings or provenance. Session paths identify historical inputs; embedded reports resolve review references durably.

reviewer.modelIdentifierLimitation: No exact model identifier is exposed in this reviewer's context. No model family or version has been inferred.
reviewer.independence: Worked from the frozen packet and public source bodies. Did not inspect author scores, prior verdicts, other reviewers' reports, session history, or live worktrees. Did not delegate.

snapshot.interpretation: Frozen candidate contents, not a claim that the additions are committed at the baseline commit.

hashVerification.method: SHA-256 of exact frozen file bytes, with byte lengths compared to snapshot.json. Runtime records independently serialized with UTF-8, ensure_ascii=false, sort_keys=true, separators=(',',':'), then SHA-256 compared with review-contract.json.
hashVerification.auxiliaryLimit: Auxiliary fingerprints identify what was read; snapshot.json does not itself provide expected hashes for these three auxiliary files.

scopeAndMethod.modeCountLimit: 83 scoped record-mode opportunities are not 83 records, independent contexts, or new-item allowances. The pilot and control are included once in their applicable counts.
completeTaskChecks: Read every owned card/expression in full, including all Japanese question text, noun labels, English en/cue, primary answers, all good/kana or writtenAnswers entries, full readingAnswers, every authored distractor, and note/explanation.
Checked the shared vocabulary entries against their occurrences, readings, inflections and contextual English glosses, not only dictionary headwords.
For Choose and Type, treated en and note as answer-side. Required state information to be present in Japanese; did not use an English explanation to repair a question.
For Read, evaluated the displayed canonical phrase together with its English en or v2 cue. Did not require readings of accepted alternative written units to be readings of the canonical display.
Applied the supplied runtime contract: normalized good precedes kana/hard, katakana folds to hiragana, and v2 performs no automatic numeral/arithmetic conversion.
Checked actual choices rather than imagining distractors that are not in the file.
Read actual public dictionary/teaching bodies and relevant PDF text; differentiated source strength, sense, numerical scope and modern-context applicability.
Assigned all 36 rubric vectors independently and counted selection evidence separately from supplied-counter transcription.

sourceEvidence.weight: Established specialist teaching reference; useful exact paradigms, not a frequency corpus or final authority on every acceptable variant.
sourceEvidence.inspected: Actual 袋/タイ, 箱, 組み, 皿, 束/ソク and 通り section prose, complete relevant number rows and examples. Relevant text recovered in two bounded page-body ranges, approximately character offsets 9000-28000.
sourceEvidence.evidence: Directly lists all packet-model native counter readings and the authored variants for 箱 1/2/6/10/何, 袋 1/2/10/14/何, 皿 8/10/何, 組 1/2/10/何, 束 1/2/10/何 and 通り 1/2/3/何. Explicitly separates school labels いちくみ/にくみ from set counts ひとくみ/ふたくみ. Distinguishes business タイ from everyday ふくろ and gives numerical and nonnumerical 一通り.
sourceEvidence.limits: Its omission of a variant is not a prohibition. Exact unusual 箱 むはこ/とはこ and 皿 とさら are supported here, not independently established as frequent. Did not turn its tendency about ソク and hundreds into a universal fixed-value rule. Its general empty-plate wording is more categorical than the packet's appropriately qualified wording.

sourceEvidence.weight: Japanese specialist counting reference; direct object/state evidence.
sourceEvidence.inspected: Heading, counting list, full 解説 and 意味.
sourceEvidence.evidence: 箱 takes 個 or 箱, 一箱 is ひとはこ, 折 and 合 have specific container contexts, and folded cardboard boxes take 枚.
sourceEvidence.limits: Does not verify all number-dependent readings or exclude ordinary generic counts. No requirement to add 折/合 when their particular container construction is not given.

sourceEvidence.inspected: Full brief counting list, 解説 and 意味.
sourceEvidence.evidence: 通常は 枚/袋; filled bags also take 個. One 袋 is ひとふくろ.
sourceEvidence.limits: The wording is not an exhaustive ban on conversational generic counts of empty bags. Does not independently establish a complete タイ paradigm.

sourceEvidence.inspected: Counting list, complete 解説 and all three noun senses.
sourceEvidence.evidence: Physical plates take 枚/個/客 with contextual qualifications; 皿 also has a served-food sense.
sourceEvidence.limits: 客 is associated with hospitality/special-occasion tableware, not every plateful. Does not equate one dish to one diner's portion.

sourceEvidence.evidence: Ordinary flower-bouquet counter 一束, explicitly ひとたば.
sourceEvidence.limits: 通常 is a preference, not exclusion of all alternatives; this entry is not a complete reading paradigm.

sourceEvidence.weight: High for lexical senses: Shogakukan Digital Daijisen and Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten, accessed through Kotobank.
sourceEvidence.inspected: Actual HTML-derived dictionary bodies for たば【束／把】, そく【束】 and つか, including Daijisen noun/counter distinction and Seisenban numbered senses. Did not rely on the leading mathematical lattice extraction.
sourceEvidence.evidence: たば counts tied collections, with flower/leek examples. そく has a bundle-unit definition and particular conventional quantities; historical paper can be 200 sheets, not universally 100. つか includes distinct old measures and other senses.
sourceEvidence.limits: Definition and historical examples do not establish equal everyday frequency of ソク and たば. They also do not require a specified modern fifty-sheet package to be silently reinterpreted as a traditional unit.

sourceEvidence.weight: High contextual reading evidence: NHK Publishing interview with a former NHK announcer; not a universal numeral-substitution rule.
sourceEvidence.inspected: Decoded the HTML-escaped JSON attributes of detail-text elements and read the complete relevant dialogue paragraph, not the title-only simplified response.
sourceEvidence.evidence: The dialogue says traditional ににんぐみ has been joined by accepted modern ふたりぐみ, which many people now use.
sourceEvidence.limits: Does not supply the 3/4-member paradigm or a JLPT assignment. No claim that every compound permits arbitrary native/Sino replacement.

sourceEvidence.weight: High for an attested pedagogical lexical item and its gloss; no JLPT authority.

sourceEvidence.limits: This reviewer did not repeat the original source author's all-pages 3-48 screening and makes no such claim. The page supplies the membership construction, not every full numerical reading or official N3 placement.

sourceEvidence.limits: The contract's local TSV, raw CSV and JMdict XML are not in this frozen review packet. Their row/sense mapping and supplied hashes were not independently re-created. A noun or homograph tag does not establish a numeric counter sense's JLPT level.

sourceEvidence.limits: Its broad wago/kango shortcuts are not exact paradigms, and some wording is overbroad. Did not mechanically manufacture イチトオリ or reject rare native 箱 forms from that shortcut. Six attempted dedicated counter URLs returned 404; those nonexistent pages are not sources.

A florist search result suggesting bouquet 本 could not be inspected because of HTTP 403 and was not used as corroboration.

retrievalLimits: Google responses were JavaScript/challenge pages; Bing returned irrelevant results for the tested Japanese queries; neither was used as linguistic evidence.
DuckDuckGo returned a human challenge; it was not bypassed.
Yahoo Japan supplied useful discovery links, but later exact-reading queries returned HTTP 429; no attempt was made to bypass rate limiting.
IMABI and long compilation pages required bounded body extraction. Kotobank simplified extraction led with a mathematical homograph; actual dictionary HTML was separately inspected.
NHK's simplified extraction returned only a title; the relevant escaped detail-text body was decoded and inspected.
Florist and HiNative HTTP 403 responses prevented body verification; snippets were not promoted to evidence.
The site's guessed /kare/ URL redirected to 枯れ葉, which was irrelevant and was not counted as curry evidence.
No pronunciation audio, pitch-accent assessment, frequency corpus or native-speaker validation was available. Only written linguistic/content claims are reviewed.

findings.claim: Read rejects the documented uncontracted pronunciation じゅうさら of displayed 十皿. The accepted list contains only じゅっさら, じっさら and とさら.
findings.reasoning: The university teaching table supplies the exact 十皿 reading; the actual public answer independently corroborates that same form. IMABI's omission is not evidence that the form is wrong. The visible party/dish cue does not require a contracted or native-only pronunciation.
findings.impact: A learner can correctly pronounce the exact displayed expression and still fail the finite Read matcher.
findings.minimumRemedy: Add じゅうさら to this record's readingAnswers; retain the valid model/contractions. Update the explanation briefly if it is intended as an exhaustive list. Do not generalize this addition to 十箱, 十袋, 十組 or 十束.
findings.confidence: High that rejection occurs under the supplied runtime contract; medium-high for linguistic acceptability, based on the exact teaching-table cell plus lower-weight corroboration.

findings.claim: The free unit/whole-count Type task omits the fitting flower-bundle counter 把/一把.
findings.reasoning: The Japanese explicitly describes five flowers tied together and handed over without untying. Sanabo's actual flower entry specifically permits 把 for bundled flowers and gives 一把 いちわ. The question does not request only 束. This is not a proposed individual-stem interpretation.
findings.impact: A documented count of the very same whole bundle is marked wrong, despite the task accepting several other non-model counters.
findings.minimumRemedy: Add 把 and 一把 to good, and the directly verified kana わ/いちわ to the appropriate typed-kana alternatives. Keep 一束 as canonical and keep its Read list separate; いちわ must not be added as a pronunciation of displayed 一束.
findings.confidence: High for fit and missing-match behavior; no claim that 把 is as common as 束.

findings.claim: The allocated paired-participants membership context is not exercised in Write/Read. The duo is a performing group; participant membership expressions use three and four members. The actual two-person participant activity asks for 二組, not 二人組.
findings.reasoning: Do not count the kumi participant group-count task as proof of the distinct 人組 operation. Generic participant membership is present, and both required readings appear elsewhere; the gap is narrow, not absence of the whole row. A numeral change alone is not extra transfer evidence, but an explicitly allocated pairing scenario still needs an appropriate owning operation if that exact context is claimed complete.
findings.impact: The completion ledger would overstate the exact paired-activity membership evidence. Learners encounter ふたりぐみ only as a performing-duo label, not the requested participant-pair label.
findings.minimumRemedy: Repurpose membership-expression-3 to an explicitly paired participant activity, with two people per group and a request for 二人組. Keep membership-expression-2 for 三人組 and membership-expression-1 for performing-group members. Alternatively explicitly revise the allocation/claim to generic participant membership rather than claim the original paired context.
findings.confidence: High about the literal inventory/operation gap; this is a contract-coverage finding, not a claim of empirical pedagogical failure.

uncertainties.claim: Whether なんはこ should also be accepted for displayed 何箱 remains unresolved.
uncertainties.known: IMABI directly lists なんばこ and なんぱこ, both already accepted. A separately inspected bare reading entry explicitly gives なんはこ, which the current finite list rejects.
uncertainties.unknown: The latter site's authority and the ordinary contextual status of the unvoiced form were not established by a reputable exact counter-table source. Subsequent targeted discovery was rate-limited.
uncertainties.impact: Potential false rejection of the displayed canonical expression; neither automatic acceptance nor a confident linguistic ban is justified from this evidence alone.
uncertainties.minimumRemedy: Seek an exact pronunciation-dictionary/established-teaching confirmation of 何箱. If confirmed, add just なんはこ. If confirmation remains unavailable, keep the Write task but defer this item's unconstrained Read opportunity, or explicitly narrow its Read cue to the voiced/p-sound forms taught here; do not silently claim the unrestricted reading list is complete.
uncertainties.confidence: High about the competing inspected strings and runtime rejection; low about the unresolved variant's status.
uncertainties.verdictEffect: hakoexpressions.json correctness is UNVERIFIED, not CLEAN.

optionalImprovements.suggestion: Retain さんとおり as the practical model and optionally label みとおり a recognized less-usual/traditional alternative. The current text does not explicitly claim equal frequency, so this is not a correctness defect.

overallVerdicts.summary: Two localized answer-acceptance defects, one narrow allocated-context gap, and one unresolved exact-reading acceptance question. No major Japanese-construction, translation, vocabulary-reading or actual wrong-choice defect was established.
overallVerdicts.cleanMeaning: No actionable defect established within the explicitly reviewed scope; not exhaustive linguistic correctness or release acceptance.

coverageAccounting.policy: Named scenario coverage, operation opportunities and conservative semantic patterns are distinct. Numerical/noun substitution, extra accepted aliases and supplied-unit v2 production do not add selection evidence. Pattern counts below are deliberately conservative judgments, not empirical transfer measurements or threshold claims.

rows.limits: Pilot package-versus-contents is merged with packed-snack-boxes, not a fourth context. Six complete moving boxes and unspecified complete boxes do not prove an empty-box context. Write cues supply 箱 and the desired number; no multiplication. U01 affects one Read answer set, not existence of the operation.

conservativeSemanticPatterns: intact filled bag rather than contents/weight
rows.limits: Rice weight and gift-piece counts are useful surface contrasts, but both Choose tasks use the same intact-package decision; do not count them as two independent package-selection patterns. タイ alternatives add recognition, not another context or industrial-unit allocation.

The control is washing tableware, not literal stocktaking; it supports the intended empty-tableware side only in Choose. Party plates do not independently demonstrate sharing. Sushi/curry and numeral changes do not multiply restaurant contexts. The actual options do not directly pit 皿 against 枚.

Class 1 and Class 2 are one label context, not two. Their cues explicitly identify labels and supply 組; they are contextual reading/transcription evidence, not independent unit selection. The participant total is stated; no calculation is necessary.

conservativeSemanticPatterns: an intact tied collection rather than its members
rows.limits: Both required material settings are present, but five flowers and fifty sheets instantiate the same semantic decision. They do not prove two independent selection strategies. No universal contents conversion or arithmetic task. F02 affects an accepted-answer boundary, not the presence of the row.

conservativeSemanticPatterns: membership size of one group, not number of groups or total people
rows.limits: Performing-duo and participant settings provide two visible scenario families, but one supplied-unit membership operation. The exact paired-participant membership operation is missing (F03). All requested member numbers are already given.

Routes/readings are the two allocated domains, not evidence of two independent counter-selection decisions. All cues supply 通り and the count/question operation. No automatic numeral conversion or combinatorial calculation.

coverageAccounting.crossRowLimits: Do not sum row-local patterns as independent mastery contexts: participant grouping is shared across 組 and 人組, and package-state contrasts recur across 箱 and 袋. There are 12 new v1 selection records plus one unchanged control; 23 v2 records supply their unit. No reverse completion is asserted.

rubric.scale: Integer 0-2 in contract order. Feedback increases with explanatory quality, not difficulty.
rubric.scoringConventions: One vector per complete record over its claimed modes, emphasizing actual question-side work. Supported but modestly unfamiliar v1 vocabulary receives 1; English v2 cues with a supplied counter generally receive lexicalLoad 0 and decisionLoad 0. Useful repetition is not a new decision. Legitimate accepted alternatives receive ambiguity 1; a consequential missing/unresolved answer receives 2. None of these tasks requires arithmetic.

inventory.review: The English cue supplies one box and explicitly excludes six contents. All three written answers fit the requested 箱 count. Both ひとはこ and いっぱこ pronounce canonical 一箱 and match the exact IMABI row; Sanabo corroborates the ordinary model. Explanation correctly distinguishes 六箱. No Japanese sentence, vocabulary block or choice distractors in this v2 record.

Japanese grammatical: twelve cookies each, unopened boxes as object, two sent. 開けずに support fits, and en is faithful. 箱/個/つ/ケース alternatives count containers; all authored kana are coherent. Read 二箱 permits ふたはこ/にはこ, not readings of 二個. Actual 枚/匹/杯 do not count these complete boxes. Twenty-four appears only in feedback; multiplication is unnecessary.

Japanese explicitly says assembled, empty and not flattened. Vocabulary covers the consequential state and movement words with correct readings/glosses. English matches. 箱/個/つ/ケース retain whole-container counting. Read 二箱 has the two checked readings. Actual 冊/匹/杯 are wrong; no need to invent an unseen 枚 choice. Feedback correctly avoids an emptiness-alone rule.

Six and 箱 are supplied; 六箱/6箱 are faithful. All three full readings ろくはこ/ろっぱこ/むはこ appear in the exact reference row. Explanation carefully says the reference records variants, not equal frequency. No ordinary-usage frequency claim verified for むはこ. 'Complete' moving boxes does not specify empty contents.

Ten boxes is explicit; twelve cookies each is irrelevant to the requested count. 十箱/10箱 and じゅっぱこ/じっぱこ/とはこ match the exact table. The calculation of 120 is feedback only, not required work. Source recognition of とはこ is not equal-frequency evidence.

Cue explicitly requests 何 and 箱, so written 何箱 is narrow and correct. Both authored Read forms なんばこ/なんぱこ are directly supported. U01 concerns a potentially missing unvoiced variant, not the validity of either listed form. The cue does not establish emptiness. Explanation correctly separates count from weight/contents.

米 is uncooked rice; supplied こめ and 開けずに gloss are correct. Two bags each containing two kilograms are explicitly distinguished in Japanese and faithful English. All 袋/個/つ forms fit whole bags. Read ふたふくろ/にたい belongs to displayed 二袋; exact IMABI supports both with register qualification. 頭/通/冊 are genuinely wrong. No 2×2 calculation needed.

Japanese establishes a complete unopened gift bag rather than one sweet; en and noun label agree. お菓子/プレゼント用/渡しました support is correct. 袋/個/つ and authored kana fit. Read 一袋 has ひとふくろ/いったい with the trade alternative expressly qualified. 頭/通/冊 do not fit; feedback explains package/content distinction.

Cue supplies ten complete rice bags and 袋. Both written answers and all four full readings match the exact 10 rows of IMABI's two paradigms. Feedback's frequency/register caveat is appropriate. No weight calculation or industrial fixed-unit claim.
Fourteen filled gift bags is clear. 十四袋/14袋 are correct; exact IMABI 14 rows verify じゅうよんふくろ/じゅうよんたい rather than inferring them only from four. Explanation does not infer a hidden gift count.
何袋 is exactly the requested question quantity. なんふくろ/なんたい are full readings of that display and explicitly in both source tables. Explanation correctly excludes the rice-weight question.

開いて平らにつぶし and 重ねました visibly establish flattened pieces before grading. Vocabulary readings/glosses fit. 枚 is supported, while 箱/個/つ remain permissible object references. Read must say にまい for 二枚; alternative box readings belong only to Type. 冊/匹/杯 are wrong. Feedback appropriately describes a preference rather than a ban.

何も入れずに平らなまま explicitly rules out filled contents; Japanese and English agree. 紙袋/平ら/棚 support is accurate. 枚 is the model, with 袋 and conversational generic counts retained; kana alternatives do not leak into Read. 一枚 is いちまい only. Actual 頭/通/杯 do not count this flat paper bag.

二人分, 大皿 and 盛って clearly describe one shared salad dish. Vocabulary ふたりぶん/おおざら/もって and glosses are correct; English preserves the two-person amount. 皿/品/つ/個 can count the single dish, but one 人前 is not silently equated with it. All listed alternative kana are plausible; Read 一皿 remains ひとさら. 頭/通/台 are wrong. Feedback states the decisive non-equivalence.

Japanese explicitly orders two of the same curry and describes both served on flat plates. 注文/平たい/盛られて readings and support are accurate; en faithful. All seven authored written unit families and their kana were considered: 皿/品/つ/個/人前/食/杯. Ordering units need not denote different menu types; 杯 is attested for curry portions and is not automatically wrong because the tableware is flat. Read 二皿 is ふたさら, not ににんまえ. 頭/通/台 are wrong. No universal serving-person equivalence is taught.

Eight platefuls of sushi and 皿 are explicitly supplied; 八皿/8皿 fit. Both はちさら and はっさら are independently corroborated by the university teaching table as well as IMABI. Feedback correctly leaves sushi-piece totals dependent on contents.

Cue and 十皿/10皿 are coherent; all three authored readings are documented. F01 identifies an additional exact displayed-form reading rejected by the finite set. Food plates versus diner count is explained well, and no arithmetic is required.
何皿 is the requested question quantity and なんさら the supported full reading. Explanation's empty-tableware 枚 contrast is qualified ('can'), not an exclusive rule.

合わせて and そろえて establish a complete cup/saucer set in Japanese; vocabulary support and en fit. All 組/組み/セット/ワンセット/式/客/つ/個 forms and authored kana were checked; 客 is specifically corroborated. Normalized セット already accepts せっと through good; no alias defect. Read 一組 is ひとくみ in the visible set context, not class-label いちくみ. 人/頭/通 are wrong; feedback explains the contrast.

Two groups of two, four altogether, are explicitly stated; number-of-groups grammar and English are correct. 全部/参加者 support fits. 組/組み/グループ/チーム/つ/個 alternatives count groups; listed kana are coherent. Read 二組 is ふたくみ in this count context. 人/枚/冊 are wrong. Feedback accurately distinguishes 二人組, but this is not itself a 人組 production task. No multiplication needed.

Visible cue explicitly selects Class 1, not one set, and excludes 第/final み. 一組/1組 and いちくみ are correct under that cue. Same written-form ambiguity is resolved on the question side. Explanation provides the contrasting ひとくみ meaning; not a class-count task.
Class 2 cue and spelling restrictions license 二組/2組 and にくみ, not ふたくみ. Feedback correctly contrasts two sets/groups. Same label-context pattern as Class 1, not another transfer context.

Ten complete matching sets is supplied. All four 組/組み plus numeral spellings fit the cue, and じゅっくみ/じっくみ match canonical 十組. Feedback correctly contrasts sets and pieces without requiring multiplication.
Cue explicitly requests number of participant groups rather than membership. 何組/何組み are coherent, and なんくみ pronounces displayed 何組. Explanation reinforces the actual requested operation.

Japanese fixes the whole tied bundle and rules out removing one flower. ひも/まとめ/ほどかずに support is correct, and en faithful. Authored 束/つ/個/本/組 counts were considered as whole-object/group references, not individual-stem alternatives; absence from one source is not a ban on 本. ひとたば is the ordinary Read model; dictionary general bundle sense and IMABI support recognition of いっそく without imposing fixed contents. F02 is the missing fitting 把 answer. 冊/人/通 are wrong. Explanation preserves the five stated flowers.

Blank sheets, fifty per tied bundle, carried intact: all conditions are Japanese question-side. しばり/白紙/運びました support is accurate. 束/つ/個/組/組み and listed kana count the two units. ふたたば/にそく read 二束 under the general bundle sense; a historical paper measure must not override explicit packaging. 人/羽/杯 are wrong. Two bundles is given, so 100 sheets is not required work.

The cue explicitly requests 束 and ten tied bundles, with no fixed internal amount. 十束/10束 and the four authored たば/そく ten-count contractions match the exact IMABI tables. Explanation does not infer hundreds of flowers. 把 is not required as an alternative written answer to a cue explicitly requesting 束.

何 and 束 are requested for tied blank-paper bundles. Written 何束 and なんたば/なんそく are coherent full forms. Feedback appropriately says check the actual package before sheet conversion, not that every historical or specialist convention is absent.

A performing duo with two members is explicit. 二人組/2人組 obey the no-final-み instruction. Actual NHK dialogue corroborates both ふたりぐみ and ににんぐみ. Feedback correctly contrasts 二組ふたくみ. This supplies performing-group membership, not the allocated participant-pair activity.

Participants form three-member groups; supplied 人組 and no-final-み instruction make 三人組/3人組 narrow. さんにんぐみ is correct. Explanation does not infer how many groups. Linguistically coherent, but a three-person group is not a paired-participants scenario.

Cue expressly asks for the four-member label, not total headcount or two groups. 四人組/4人組 and よにんぐみ are correct. Eight people occurs only in feedback; no arithmetic is required. F03 is a proposed repurposing for the missing allocated pair context, not an error in the existing 四人組 expression.

Exactly one route and the numerical operation are visible; the nonnumerical meaning is explicitly excluded. 一通り/1通り and ひととおり fit. Feedback accurately distinguishes the other lexical meaning. Supplied 通り means no independent unit-selection task.

Two possible readings is an actual alternatives count. 二通り/2通り fit; ふたとおり/にとおり are supported by IMABI and the library's exact NHK-table report. Neither reads 通つう or describes streets. No route/reading enumeration is needed from the learner.

Three routes and 通り are supplied. 三通り/3通り and さんとおり/みとおり match the exact IMABI row; the specialist dictionary separately recognizes both readings. No equal-frequency claim established. Explanation rules out combinatorics, but does not add another selection operation.

The alternative-reading question explicitly requests 何 and 通り. 何通り and なんとおり are correct; feedback's contrast with 何通なんつう counts actual messages/letters, not the alternatives. Supplied-unit question expression, not independent choice or arithmetic.

白いお皿を一{}洗いました is natural and en faithfully means washing one white plate. Physical tableware is established by washing, without needing the answer-side noun gloss to supply a serving condition. Among actual 枚/人/匹/冊 choices only 枚 fits. No separate explanatory note, hence feedback 0. Typed alternatives, Read expansion and newly-N3 status are outside this control's claim.
